# Tisonik

Tisonik is operated by TSquare Ventures LLC, a Wyoming (USA) limited liability company. Tisonik provides guest-experience activation for cruise lines and all-inclusive hotels and resorts.

## What Tisonik is
Tisonik is designed as a white-label guest-experience interaction layer that fits inside an operator's existing digital journey rather than replacing the operator's core app, PMS, booking or commerce stack.

For all-inclusive hotels and resorts, Tisonik focuses on experience discovery and participation, relevant ancillary-revenue opportunities, in-stay ratings and service recovery, and staff recognition.

## Resort product boundaries
- Tisonik is an experience layer, not a replacement for the resort's core operational or commerce systems.
- Resort inventory, availability, pricing, checkout, payment and fulfilment remain with the resort.
- Public demonstrations and demo metrics are illustrative and do not imply a hotel or resort affiliation or production performance.
- The in-stay rating flow is designed to take no more than about five minutes.
- The rating product uses exactly 10 standard questions; participating hotels do not choose, replace or rewrite them.
- Questions 1–8 are fixed guest pain-point questions and use a 1–10 score.
- Question 9 is “What was good?” and allows up to 400 characters.
- Question 10 is “What could be improved?” and allows up to 400 characters.
- The purpose of in-stay ratings is to give the resort a chance to respond while the guest is still on property or before departure.
- Participation means publication: submitted ratings go public, and a participating property cannot selectively suppress or hold back poor ratings.
- Relevant paid experiences can include spa and wellness, speciality dining, excursions, cabanas and daybeds, private transfers, celebrations and watersports.
- Tisonik surfaces these opportunities in context while inventory, pricing, checkout, payment and fulfilment remain with the resort.
- Public commercial-performance claims should follow real pilot evidence rather than demo assumptions.

## Cruise product boundaries
- Tisonik is designed as an add-on interaction layer inside the cruise line's existing app, not a replacement for the cruise line's app or core commerce stack.
- Inventory, pricing, checkout and payment remain with the cruise line.
- The default analytics architecture accepts only a predefined aggregate report from the cruise-line environment; it has no passenger/crew source-event endpoint.
- Passenger and crew privacy, recognition, recovery and aggregate-measurement boundaries are described in the extended public reference.
